title: The Civilizational Layer
subtitle: From Ambient Coordination to Civilizational Carrying Capacity
author: Raynor Eissens
description: A conceptual bridge linking RFL-5's civilizational ambient coordination layer to later work on carrying layers, superartifacts and civilizational carrying capacity.
thesis: A civilization can itself become a carrying layer.
core_proposition: A civilization can itself become a carrying layer.

lineage.relationship: Longitudinal synthesis rather than an additive new layer.

sequence: RFL-1 through RFL-4 scale coordination outward from person to relation to household to civic field.
RFL-5 marks the point where those fields interoperate into a civilizational ambient layer.
The carrying layer models how systems absorb practical complexity without continually transferring reconstruction costs to human attention.
Superartifacts provide a model for addressable, lineage-preserving capability across changing implementations.
Improving intelligence may increase the density of coherent research and transformation civilization can sustain per unit of time.
closing_sequence: Improved intelligence increases what the civilization can carry.

references.citation: Raynor Eissens (2026), RFL-5 — Civilizational Ambient Coordination.
Raynor Eissens (2026), The Artifact Layer of the Intelligence Stack.
Raynor Eissens (2026), When the Carrier Improves Itself.

evidence_boundary: Conceptual synthesis across the author's own corpus. The article does not establish that a civilizational ambient layer exists or that this trajectory is inevitable.
